name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,536

clue.text: Lovers crossing old river to get Dutch wine

indicators.note: the lovers stretch across the old river and the Dutch, so those pieces sit inside the lovers

explanation.surface: Two lovers cross an old river to buy wine from the Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: The lovers' word splits after its first letter to take in old, river and Dutch together. The wine is French, not Dutch: 'Dutch' only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is the red or white wine produced around the French city and region of that name.

clue.text: Intense lamentation for the dead

blocks.note: adjective: strong or eager, as of feeling or interest

explanation.surface: Mourners grieve fiercely at a funeral.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, but splits after 'Intense': an adjective, then a noun meaning the Irish funeral wail.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes strong, eager feeling; as a noun it names a traditional Irish wailing dirge sung over a corpse.

clue.text: Animal covering women in surgery in dung

indicators.note: the animal wraps around the whole surgery with its woman inside
women placed within the operation, so 'surgery' holds 'women'

explanation.surface: An animal in a vet's surgery ends up covered in dung.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: women inside surgery, then that inside the animal. The two uses of 'in' differ: the first places a letter, the second joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpat is a flat round dropping of cattle manure, a specific kind of dung found in fields.

clue.text: Supplementary material produced by clergyman replacing leader of group in schedule

indicators.note: the clergyman takes the place of the group's leader in the schedule

blocks.note: Doctor of Divinity, a clergyman's degree

explanation.surface: A vicar's extra notes get slipped into the meeting schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the G of AGENDA for DD. DD (Doctor of Divinity) is the usual crossword clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda, plural of addendum, are extra sections appended to a book or document to supply further information.

clue.text: Useless deli in difficulties

indicators.note: a deli in trouble is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling delicatessen is dismissed as a failure.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters of 'deli' rearrange. 'Useless' is a fair sense: idle threats or talk achieve nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or without effect, as in idle speculation, which matches worthless or pointless.

clue.text: Foreign lads end run in UK city

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters appear in an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: Overseas young men finish a run in a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: All ten letters of 'lads end run' rearrange. Sunderland is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is a port city on the River Wear in Tyne and Wear, north-east England.

clue.text: Setter with ghastly headache

explanation.surface: The crossword setter suffers a terrible headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' means the compiler, so ME; 'with' just joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Megrim is an old word for migraine, a severe one-sided pain in the head.

clue.text: Three dimensional body protecting one twisted coil of wire

indicators.note: turning 'one' around makes it read backwards
the body guards 'one' by wrapping around it

blocks.note: a solid in geometry has three dimensions

explanation.surface: A 3D shape shields a bent item from harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three dimensional body' is a geometric solid, not a person's body; 'coil of wire' is the definition, not the item twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A solenoid is a cylindrical winding of wire that acts as an electromagnet when current flows through it.

clue.text: Priest cutting awfully rude fruit with stone

indicators.note: done awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled
the priest cuts into the rude letters, ending up inside them

explanation.surface: A cleric slices up rude fruit that has a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: RUDE rearranges to DRUE, and P slips in before the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A drupe is the botanical term for a fleshy fruit, like a plum or cherry, enclosing a single hard pit.

clue.text: Editor given space in paradise

blocks.note: a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: An editor gets some room in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a printing unit of space; 'given' tacks it onto ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived, used generally for any perfect place of bliss.

clue.text: Bow during new prayer to resident clergyman

indicators.note: a new version of prayer has its letters remade
the bow happens within the prayer, so it sits inside

blocks.note: to bow is to bend at the waist

explanation.surface: Someone bows while saying a new prayer to the local vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAYER rearranges to PRE-ARY, with BEND placed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A prebendary is a canon of a cathedral who receives a stipend, a clergy member attached to that church.

clue.text: Bringer of good luck for member at racecourse

blocks.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire

explanation.surface: A lucky charm is carried by someone at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places M directly beside the racecourse. Ascot is the English racecourse of Royal Ascot fame.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object adopted by a team or group as a charm thought to attract good fortune.

clue.text: Committee to meet in session hosted by destitute printer's employee

indicators.note: a guest sits inside the host's home, so 'meet in session' goes inside 'destitute'

blocks.note: a court or parliament sits when it is in session

explanation.surface: A committee session is funded by a penniless printer's worker.
explanation.walkthrough: COM is the usual abbreviation for committee; the session verb goes inside POOR, splitting it PO-OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor was the skilled worker in a print shop who arranged metal type into pages ready for printing.

clue.text: Vessels covering former parts of ocean tricky for sailors

definitions.text: parts of ocean tricky for sailors

indicators.note: the vessels wrap round 'former', holding it inside

blocks.note: former and old both mean of an earlier time

explanation.surface: Ships sail over once-charted seas that are hard to navigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, but here they are containers such as oil drums.
explanation.definitionFit: The doldrums are equatorial ocean belts of calm, windless weather where sailing ships could be stranded for weeks.

clue.text: See 17
Letter prefacing generous pattern

indicators.note: to preface is to come before, so the letter goes in front of 'generous'

blocks.note: the spelt-out name of the letter X
a generous helping is an ample one

explanation.surface: A letter heads a model of generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is not a single character but a letter's name written out: EX for X, as EF is F or EM is M.
explanation.definitionFit: An example can be a model to copy or imitate, the same sense as a pattern to follow.

clue.text: Keep out of the public eye in speaker's bed

definitions.text: Keep out of the public eye

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, not seen, so the bed's word counts by its sound

blocks.note: a Lilo is an inflatable airbed, a British brand name

explanation.surface: Someone hides away from publicity by staying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lilo is a British inflatable mattress used on beaches or when camping; said aloud it matches the two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for hiding or keeping quiet so as to avoid attention or discovery.

clue.text: Have faith in variable source of aphrodisiac in concoctions from the east

indicators.note: the source is where something starts, so take the opening letter of 'aphrodisiac'
the chosen letter is placed within 'concoctions'
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z as variables
brews are mixed drinks or potions

explanation.surface: Someone trusts in potions containing a love drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Y then BR(A)EWS forms YBRAEWS, which is then read backwards. Blocks are listed before the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear by something is an idiom meaning to trust it completely and recommend it as reliable.

clue.text: Country wasn't prepared to stop snake

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
a stopper plugs the inside of a bottle, so the jumbled letters go inside 'snake'

blocks.note: a boa is a constricting snake

explanation.surface: A nation was not ready to halt a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasn't prepared' reads as one phrase meaning unready, but 'prepared' is the anagram signal working on 'wasn't'.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a landlocked nation in southern Africa, bordered by South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe.

clue.text: Usher set off to part of hospital

indicators.note: food gone off is spoiled, so 'set' is in a spoiled order

blocks.note: a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: An usher heads off towards a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' reads as 'departed', but 'set' is the fodder and 'off' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward guides people to their places at an event, just as an usher shows people to their seats.

clue.text: Devil over shelter is powerless

blocks.note: an imp is a small devil
O for over, as in cricket scoring
a tent is a portable shelter

explanation.surface: A demon standing over a refuge has lost its strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is not a positional instruction but supplies a letter: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over, a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means lacking force, strength or effectiveness, the same as having no ability to act.

clue.text: Soldiers eaten by nasty mythological sea creature

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so the soldiers go inside 'nasty'

explanation.surface: Troops are devoured by a vicious legendary sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: RM (Royal Marines) is a standard crossword set of soldiers. 'nasty' looks like a description of the monster, but it is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A merman is the male counterpart of a mermaid, a legendary being with a human torso and a fish's tail.

clue.text: Quiet country residence accommodating duke and earl

indicators.note: a house accommodating a guest has it inside, so the residence holds 'duke'

blocks.note: a country seat is an aristocrat's rural mansion

explanation.surface: A peaceful stately home plays host to a duke and an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the duke goes inside; 'and earl' is added on at the end. A seat is the grand family house of landed gentry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, unhurried and dignified, matching quiet in the sense of subdued or tranquil.

clue.text: Small robin primarily found in brownish-purple tree

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of 'robin' is taken
the robin's letter is located within the colour

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A little robin is spotted in a dark reddish tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brownish-purple' reads as describing the tree, but it names the colour puce, from the French for flea.
explanation.definitionFit: A spruce is a conifer with needle-like leaves and hanging cones, the common Christmas tree species.

clue.text: Ability to water tip of plant in shady part of garden

indicators.note: the tip of a plant is its end, here taken as the opening letter
the watering and the plant tip go within the garden's shady spot

blocks.note: a bower is a leafy, shaded garden retreat

explanation.surface: A gardener's skill at watering plants in a shady corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' here is a verb meaning to rain, and it goes with the P inside BOWER after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainpower is mental capacity or intelligence, a kind of intellectual ability or capability.

clue.text: Look part of castle over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the castle part is read backwards up the grid

blocks.note: a keep is the central fortified tower of a castle

explanation.surface: Someone glances over a section of a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' suggests inspecting; here 'over' is the reversal signal and 'Look' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick, often secret glance, so it works as a noun or verb matching look.

clue.text: Unit housing western urban centre

indicators.note: a building housing someone has them inside, so the unit holds 'western'

blocks.note: a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A housing block in a western city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unit housing' suggests a flat or apartment block, but 'housing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a built-up populated settlement, larger than a village, which is an urban centre.

clue.text: Nonsense talked by drunk turning up at hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
standard abbreviation, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A drunk arrives at hospital babbling rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the reversed drunkard next to H.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosh is British slang for rubbish or foolish talk, as in 'utter tosh'.

clue.text: Difficulty with extremely brittle building material

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters of 'brittle' count

explanation.surface: Trouble with very fragile construction stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'brittle' but selects its ends; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick, used for houses in hot, dry regions such as the American south-west.

clue.text: Dissenter's angry tirade about old French coins

indicators.note: the tirade goes round the coins, holding them inside

blocks.note: a rant is an angry outburst
the ecu was a French silver or gold coin

explanation.surface: A protester furiously denounces old French money.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay rather than a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A recusant is someone who refuses to obey an authority, historically a Catholic refusing Church of England services.
